subject: Next steps: deployment path, PHI flow & evidence needed
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@cardioai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0000
Subject: Post-call recap — deployment path, PHI flow & evidence needed

Thanks Elena — great conversation today. Recap and concrete asks below so we have alignment and a clear next-MAP: 

Quick recap
- CardioAI wants LLM-powered triage and note-summarization for cardiac patient intake; some inputs will include PHI (name, DOB, MRN).
- Preference: Dedicated capacity in-cardioai VPC if possible, but legal is evaluating whether a full on-prem requirement will be enforced for the highest-risk subset.
- Compliance asks: BAA required; SOC 2 Type II evidence; customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest is preferred.

Immediate asks (what we need from CardioAI to size & scope):
1) Data flow diagram showing which fields contain PHI and which requests may be routed off-prem. (attachment suggested)
2) Monthly token estimate (peak qps and average). You mentioned ~1.5M tokens/day — please confirm typical burst windows.
3) Retention and audit window requirements (how long logs/traces must be retained for audits).
4) Procurement timeline and PO/contract owner for BAA sign-off.

What Redwood will deliver / proposed MAP items
- Provide SOC2 artifact index and BAA template (attached).
- Technical plan for Dedicated VPC peering + KMS integration and estimated lead time.
- Proposal for a 30-day Dedicated POC (isolated pool, same SLA as Dedicated) so security can validate operations.

Proposed next steps / dates
- Please send the data flow diagram + token numbers by EOD Wed Aug 31 so we can finalize sizing.
- We will assemble a SOC2 artifact bundle and a BAA draft by Fri Sep 3.
- Proposed follow-up call: Thu Sep 2 at 10:00am PT with Legal + Infra (30 min).

Attachments: redwood_baa_summary.pdf, soc2-artifact-index.pdf (artifact index is high level).

Thanks — I’ve looped in Karthik for infra sizing and Sean for the procurement/finance signals.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Elena Park <elena.park@cardioai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 14:42:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment path, PHI flow & evidence needed

Thanks Marissa — super clear, appreciate the recap. A few clarifications and answers inline: 

Data flow / PHI
- We attached a simple data flow (cardioai_data_flow_v1.png) to this reply. Primary PHI: patient name, DOB, MRN, diagnostic images references (links). Note: ~70% of incoming messages are low-risk (no identifiers), but ~30% have identifiers that Legal insists be handled inside our VPC or on-prem.

Volume estimates
- Average: 1.2M tokens/day. Peak windows coincide with 9am–11am ET and 3pm–4pm ET; peak qps ~220.

Retention / audit
- We need logs and audit evidence retained for 7 years for certain cases (per contract). For initial SOC2 review, 90-day access to operational logs is sufficient, but legal may later request full retention.

Hosting preference & constraints
- Preferred: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering into our AWS account (customer-managed KMS).
- Fallback: on-prem appliance for the subset of requests that include high-risk PHI (this would be a later phase — procurement is cautious about on-prem).

Procurement timeline
- Legal: aiming to complete BAA review by Sep 17. Procurement/PO expected by Oct 1 if BAA approved.

Attachments: cardiaoai_data_flow_v1.png (diagram)

Would be helpful if Redwood can confirm: 
1) Whether Dedicated VPC peering + customer KMS is supported end-to-end (and a high-level lead time).
2) If BAA + SOC2 artifact package will allow our security team to sign-off for a Dedicated POC without requiring on-prem immediately.

Happy to take the Sep 2 meeting — I’ll invite Legal and our Infra lead.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Security & Compliance | CardioAI
elena.park@cardioai.com | +1 212-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@cardioai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment path, PHI flow & evidence needed

Elena — great, thanks for the data flow and numbers. Quick answers and a concrete MAP so your team and Legal can track deliverables: 

Quick answers (short)
- Dedicated VPC peering + customer-managed KMS: supported. KMS integration requires IAM roles and a KMS key policy review; we can support AWS KMS key rotation and customer key access controls. Estimated setup lead time: 10 business days for KMS config + 20 business days for VPC peering and network validation (parallel work can shorten calendar time).
- BAA + SOC2 artifacts: we will produce an artifact bundle and a draft BAA; SRE/Infra will support the POC without needing on-prem if Legal accepts the artifact bundle and KMS controls.

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — target dates (helpful to list ownership)
1) CardioAI: Send final data-flow + confirm exact token estimate and any additional retention requirements — due Wed Sep 1 — OWNER: Elena.
2) Redwood: Share SOC2 artifact bundle + BAA draft — due Fri Sep 3 — OWNER: Marissa. (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-soc2-cardioai)
3) Redwood infra: Prepare Dedicated POC runbook (network diagram, KMS steps, expected ops SLOs) — due Mon Sep 6 — OWNER: Karthik.
4) Joint call: Thu Sep 2, 10:00am PT — Legal + Infra — confirm whether POC can proceed without on-prem.
5) If Legal approves: Redwood to provision 30-day Dedicated POC environment and send onboarding guide — target Sep 10.

Cost note (ballpark)
- Dedicated POC: estimated incremental monthly run-rate for Dedicated pool at proposed scale: ~$18k–25k/month (final quote after we confirm concurrency and model selection).

Next meeting: Confirmed Thu Sep 2 10:00am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda (legal + infra validation, BAA timeline, POC acceptance criteria).

Quoting your note below for visibility:

> Primary PHI: patient name, DOB, MRN, diagnostic images references (links). ~30% have identifiers that Legal insists be handled inside our VPC or on-prem.

Thanks — looping in Karthik and Sean for the infra and procurement details.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Internal: infra notes / lead times for CardioAI Dedicated + KMS

Internal notes for the Sep 2 call (posting here so Marissa & Sean have a concise list):

Summary of technical options we can offer
- Option A (preferred fast path): Dedicated pool with VPC peering into CardioAI AWS account. Requests that contain identifiers remain in the peered VPC; routing by request header. Supports customer-managed AWS KMS for disk encryption and object encryption.
- Option B (hybrid): Host low-risk requests on Redwood hosted nodes; route high-risk PHI to CardioAI peered Dedicated nodes or on-prem appliance. Adds routing complexity but reduces cost for CardioAI at scale.
- Option C (on-prem): Full on-prem install — highest effort and procurement friction; plan only if Legal insists after reviewing artifacts.

Lead times (rough)
- KMS integration (IAM roles / key policy review / test): ~10 business days assuming CardioAI provides KMS ARN and an IAM test role.
- VPC peering + network validation + firewall rules: ~15–20 business days (depends on CardioAI network ops availability).
- POC environment provisioning and runbook creation: 5 business days after network approvals.

Required artifacts for Security review
- SOC2 artifact index (we will provide)
- Encryption key custodian matrix + KMS key policy sample (we will provide templates)
- Network topology and peering checklist (we will produce)

Action items (internal)
- Marissa: finalize BAA draft delivery Sep 3.
- Sean: prep procurement checklist & estimate for POC cost center.
- Karthik: draft Dedicated POC runbook and KMS integration steps by Sep 6.

I’ll bring a short tech slide to the Sep 2 call to walk Legal through KMS flow and routing options. If CardioAI can confirm token numbers by Sep 1 we can give them a final cost/quote on the call.

—Karthik

Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
